newsitem.title: USA: MSRB exec says pay-to-play not gone underground.
newsitem.headline: MSRB exec says pay-to-play not gone underground.

text.p: The Municipal Securities Rulemaking Board's (MSRB) top staffer said the board's tough curbs on political contributions in the municipal market will not lead to more covert giving such as bribery and kickbacks by dealers to municipal officials.
Christopher Taylor, executive director of the MSRB, said getting convicted of bribery and kickbacks is a "death sentence" for bond firms.

"If people are doing bribes and kickbacks behind the scenes, it is clearly a violation of public corruption laws and a whole lot of other things," Taylor told reporters after addressing municipal analysts meeting here this week.
"If a dealer is found guilty of a felony, it might as well close up shop," Taylor said.

"It can't deal with any public body in any line of business. Even if they are running a mutual fund in their company, they are deregistered automatically in a bunch of states. It's a death sentence," Taylor said.

The Miami Herald reported Sept. 26 that Calvin Grigsby, president of Grigsby Brandford & Co. was shown on videotape allegedly offering a $300,000 bribe to a Dade County, Fla., official in exchange for county bond business.

Grigsby resigned Sept. 17 and has not been available for comment. No charges have been filed against Grigsby whose attorney has maintained that he is innocent. The firm's two remaining partners, Napoleon Brandford and Suzanne Shank, announced this week they will join New York securities firm Muriel Siebert & Co.
